summary.intent: Run the GSD plan-phase and execute-phase workflows for cipher-box phase 68.2 (SDK-owned read chain and resolved folder listings) end-to-end, and stand up a parallel worktree to start phase 69 independently.
summary.outcome: Phase 68.2 planning completed fully (research, Nyquist VALIDATION.md, D-07 scope resolved to full boundary, pattern-map, SDK-READ-01..04 registered, 12 plans/7 waves, plan-checker PASSED, all coverage gates green) and execution proceeded sequentially through Wave 1 (SDK read-path gate), Wave 2 (ResolvedChild listing API), and into Wave 3 (write facade landed, desync e2e dispatched); a clean origin/main worktree for phase 69 was also created at cipher-box-phase69.

repo: gsd-tools query commit reports a 'commit_failed' false negative even on ordinary commits (not just reword) — always verify with git log before treating it as a real failure; happened for VALIDATION.md and for plan-01's final metadata commit.

worktree.baseRef config determines whether executor worktrees fork from live HEAD or origin/main ('fresh' default) — must be verified as 'head' before dispatching worktree executors, otherwise they'd miss local commits (e.g. all 12 PLAN.md files) not yet pushed to origin.

In this pnpm monorepo, worktree-based parallel execution is often not worth it: each worktree needs its own pnpm install (expensive), and when most waves are single-plan, sequential execution on the main tree gives identical correctness (same-wave plans are file-disjoint) with far less fragility.

GSD executors sometimes prematurely mark a requirement's checkbox '[x]' in REQUIREMENTS.md when their plan's tasks pass, even though the requirement's acceptance criteria depend on a later plan (e.g. deleting orphaned services in Wave 6) — needs manual spot-checking/reverting after each wave until the true completing plan lands.

The gap-analysis.plan-post check's JSON output can contain control characters in the 'rendered' field that break naive parsing — run the check directly rather than relying on the wrapped query output.

git fetch can fail in a sandboxed session (no network) but a locally cached origin/main ref can still be current/valid if it matches the known fork-base of an active feature branch created that same day.

code.finding: RotationHighWater.enforceResolved gate added to resolvePublishedNode (root resolve) as part of closing the SDK's zero-gating read-path pitfall (ROT-07).
enforceResolved gate also added inside dfsFindFolder's child loop; pre-existing write-path gate remains at line 1156.

resolveChildren's per-child skip-on-failure degradation is security-sound: the target folder is already gated via ensureFolderLoaded/dfsFindFolder before this runs, so an unverifiable sibling is simply omitted (availability tradeoff) rather than rendered with stale/attacker content; caller's parentReadKey is never zeroed here, minted childReadKey is zeroed in a finally block.

workflow: For sequential (non-worktree) multi-wave execution, independently spot-check and re-run acceptance/security tests after each wave rather than trusting the subagent's self-reported PASS, especially for security-critical plans.

When a subagent reports a 'notable deviation' on security-adjacent code, read the actual implementation/docstring reasoning before accepting the deviation as safe, rather than accepting the executor's own justification at face value.

When the roadmap marks a dependency between phases as 'design-mirroring' rather than a code dependency, it's reasonable to start the dependent phase's worktree off origin/main and rely on cross-branch reads (git show <branch>:path) to reference the other phase's docs instead of blocking on merge.

friction: gsd-tools commit helper's spurious 'commit_failed' result required manual git log verification multiple times across the session, adding extra steps despite being a known/documented issue.
git fetch failed outright from the sandboxed session, forcing reliance on a possibly-stale local origin/main ref (verified safe only by cross-checking against the current branch's fork point).
REQUIREMENTS.md checkbox state drifted from actual completion status after Wave 1 and Wave 2 (SDK-READ-01/02 marked '[x]' prematurely), requiring manual detection and reversion mid-execution.
gap-analysis.plan-post's rendered JSON field contained control characters that broke the standard query parser, requiring a fallback to running the check directly.
open_items: D-03 poll-invalidation path still lacks automated behavioral test coverage (only grep/typecheck); logged as todo .planning/todos/pending/2026-07-06-d03-poll-invalidation-lacks-automated-coverage.md for follow-up after phase completion.

SDK-READ-01, 02, and 04 requirements remain '[ ]' in REQUIREMENTS.md pending Wave 6 (plan 11) deletion of orphaned web services (ipns.service.ts, file-metadata.service.ts, kind-cache.ts, useFileSize.ts) — must be flipped to '[x]' when that lands.
